text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today and has lost 11% over the past two weeks, tracking a sharp decline in oil prices driven by easing geopolitical tensions. On November 10th, crude dropped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August after President Trump signaled the Iran conflict was winding down, reducing the risk premium that had kept prices elevated. With Brent crude down and US oil at $99.64 (well below the $107 world price), the stock reflects weaker margins and lower energy valuations across the sector.

The timing coincides with ConocoPhillips' quarterly earnings announcement on November 5th—a potential trigger for selling if results or guidance disappointed investors given the oil price backdrop, though the broader driver is clearly the shift in geopolitical risk and crude's downward reset.
